purpose: PR0-C: inventory of every evaluation path in RagingBoltPolicy (+ the standalone value model), so their inputs/outputs/units/terminal-value handling/callers can be compared on the SAME snapshot (shadow comparison) without unifying them or changing any decision. No policy change is implied by this document.

evaluate_state.granularity: per-STATE (the current board only) -- not per-action, not per-candidate
inputs: self.me / self.opponent (current board: prizes, active/bench Pokemon + energies, hand)
evaluate_state.output_unit: raw linear-eval score, unscaled (weights are hundreds, so typical magnitude is low hundreds to low thousands)
evaluate_state.terminal_value_handling: none -- no special-casing for a game-ending state; not designed to be called on a terminal SearchState at all (it reads self.me/self.opponent, which come from the live Observation, not a simulated end state)
evaluate_state.decision_effect_source: PR0-A.1 (verified independently: `current_eval` appears exactly once in main.py, at its own assignment)
evaluate_state.reachability: computed every time the heuristic-blend fallback in choose_with_search() runs (use_engine_search=0, OR select.maxCount != 1 so _engine_search_choose() early-returns None, OR an exception fell through to the fallback) -- the computation happens, the result is discarded
evaluate_state.notes: Reads like it was intended as a baseline/reference score to compare future_delta against, but no such comparison exists in the current code. All 19 eval_* params are dead weight under every current-config path.

_eval_search_state.granularity: per-CANDIDATE -- called once per rollout, on the SearchState produced by rolling one specific candidate action forward (via _rollforward) to the search horizon
inputs: state: a cg.api SearchState (engine's simulated post-rollforward board), NOT the live Observation

_extract_eval_features(state, my_index): se_prize_taken, se_prize_given, se_closing, se_opp_closing, se_field_energy, se_bolt_ready, se_can_ko, se_bench_bolt_ready, se_active_dies_prize, se_active_dies_energy, se_no_backup, se_disabled, se_dot, se_opp_damage, se_my_damage, se_bench_damage*, se_bench_ko_risk* (see main.py:1546-1630 for the full feature block; not all se_* keys are listed in the PR0-A audit's static _EVAL_FEATURE_WEIGHTS dump, since some are added conditionally)
_eval_search_state.param_keys: self.p(k, self._EVAL_FEATURE_WEIGHTS[k]) for every key k in the extracted feature dict -- see _EVAL_FEATURE_WEIGHTS class attribute for the code-default weight of each se_* key
_eval_search_state.output_unit: raw linear-eval score in the SAME nominal units as evaluate_state() (feature * weight, weights are tens-to-hundreds) EXCEPT for the terminal special case below -- the two are NOT on a verified-comparable scale (see shadow comparison caveat)
_eval_search_state.terminal_value_handling: EXPLICIT and LARGE: state is None -> 0.0; state.result >= 0 (game decided) -> +1,000,000.0 if I won, -1,000,000.0 if I lost. This is ~1000x the typical non-terminal feature-score magnitude -- by design, a terminal outcome must dominate any non-terminal comparison in the same rollout batch.

callers.caller: _engine_search_choose.rollout_once (used by both the legacy flat-allocation path and _ucb1_choose)
callers.consumption: consumed -- feeds directly into the UCB1 value estimate / legacy averaged total for the candidate

_eval_search_state.decision_effect: STATICALLY_DECISION_RELEVANT and (unlike evaluate_state) actually reachable under the live config (use_engine_search=1, rule_ucb1_search=1)
_eval_search_state.reachability: every rollout of every MAIN-context, select.maxCount==1 decision -- the dominant decision path in the live agent
_eval_search_state.notes: Subject to the PR0-B empirical finding: NOT deterministic given identical materialized hidden samples, because state comes from search_begin/search_step with manual_coin=False (engine's own internal RNG for any coin-flip effect hit during rollforward). See audit/crn_capability_matrix.json.

_estimate_action_impact.granularity: per-CANDIDATE -- a cheap, pure-Python heuristic delta for one specific option, no engine call, no rollforward
inputs: self state (active/bench energies, hand, bolt_ready, bt_total_energy, opp_active_hp, etc.)
_estimate_action_impact.output_unit: raw linear-eval delta, same rough order of magnitude as evaluate_state()/_score_option (tens to low thousands) -- no explicit unit reconciliation with either
_estimate_action_impact.terminal_value_handling: none -- estimates a state CHANGE, not an absolute state or terminal outcome

callers.consumption: consumed -- blended into `final = immediate*w_imm + future_delta*w_fut + risk_adj*w_risk`, which DOES determine the returned ranking in this fallback branch

_estimate_action_impact.decision_effect: STATICALLY_DECISION_RELEVANT, but ONLY inside the same fallback branch as evaluate_state() (use_engine_search=0, OR select.maxCount != 1, OR an engine-search exception) -- unlike evaluate_state, this one's result IS actually consumed when that branch runs
_estimate_action_impact.reachability: fallback branch only -- rare in the common single-action MAIN decision (maxCount==1) case where engine search succeeds, more relevant for any select.maxCount != 1 MAIN decision (e.g. multi-select contexts) which always skip engine search entirely (_engine_search_choose returns None immediately for maxCount != 1)
_estimate_action_impact.notes: Never directly shadow-comparable against _eval_search_state's rollforward-based value without running the SAME engine rollforward for a same-footing comparison; comparable in principle against _score_option's immediate score (same candidate, same fallback branch, both consumed together in `final`).

_score_option (+ per-type _score_play /.signature: self._score_option(i, opt) -> float (called for every option in self.select.option via self.rank())
_score_option (+ per-type _score_play /.granularity: per-CANDIDATE, purely heuristic, no engine call
inputs: opt (every legal option for the current select, not just top-k)
_score_option (+ per-type _score_play /.param_keys: score_* keys (97 ACTIVE + several UNUSED, per PR0-A audit/parameter_contract.json) plus 133 hardcoded numeric literals bypassing self.p() entirely (see audit/hardcoded_score_inventory.json)
_score_option (+ per-type _score_play /.output_unit: raw linear-eval score, same nominal family as the others but never cross-calibrated against them

callers.consumption: consumed -- this IS the ranking used everywhere: as the heuristic pre-filter for engine-search candidates (top_k), as the sole ranking in choose() for all non-MAIN contexts, and as `immediate` inside the fallback blend

_score_option (+ per-type _score_play /.decision_effect: STATICALLY_DECISION_RELEVANT and reachable on EVERY decision (MAIN and non-MAIN alike) -- this is the one evaluator that is unconditionally on the critical path
_score_option (+ per-type _score_play /.notes: Because this is always computed and always at least partially consumed (as the top_k candidate PRE-FILTER for engine search, even when the engine search's own _eval_search_state ultimately picks the final action), any shadow comparison should treat _score_option's ranking as the reference ranking that the other evaluators are compared against, not as a peer on equal footing.

value_model.predict_action_value / predi.signature: predict_action_value(obs, my_index, opt) -> float | None (win probability, sklearn predict_proba); predict_state_value(obs, my_index) -> float | None
value_model.predict_action_value / predi.granularity: per-CANDIDATE (predict_action_value) or per-STATE (predict_state_value, currently unused by main.py's decision path)
inputs: obs (live Observation, NOT a rolled-forward SearchState)
feature_extractor.extract_features() -- a DIFFERENT feature set than _extract_eval_features (se_*) or evaluate_state's inline features
value_model.predict_action_value / predi.output_unit: WIN PROBABILITY in [0, 1] -- fundamentally different unit from every other evaluator in this matrix (they are all unscaled linear-eval score units). choose_with_search blends it in as `v * value_model_weight * 1000`, an ad hoc unit conversion with no calibration evidence on record.
value_model.predict_action_value / predi.terminal_value_handling: implicit only, via whatever the trained classifier learned from labeled game outcomes -- no explicit override

callers.caller: choose_with_search (heuristic-blend fallback, inside the value_model branch)
callers.consumption: consumed when use_value_model is truthy AND the fallback branch runs AND the model files load successfully

value_model.predict_action_value / predi.decision_effect: STATICALLY_DECISION_RELEVANT in principle, but DISABLED_BY_CURRENT_CONFIG (use_value_model=false in the live params.json, per PR0-A.1)
value_model.predict_action_value / predi.notes: value_model.pkl / value_model_meta.json exist on disk in experiments/agents/raging_bolt/ but are not loaded in production because the gate is off. Its win-probability unit and the ad hoc *1000 conversion are the single largest scale-mismatch risk in this matrix if it is ever re-enabled without a calibration pass.

web/counterfactual_analyzer.py:analyze_c.granularity: OFFLINE, across many saved human-vs-AI disagreement traces (session_tuning_log.jsonl) -- not invoked during any live decision
inputs: saved Live Tuning Panel trace files (JSONL), not a live Observation or SearchState
web/counterfactual_analyzer.py:analyze_c.output_unit: categorical judgment (recommend/consider/skip-family labels) + aggregate counters, not a numeric board-state score

callers.caller: CLI / Live Tuning Panel review workflow only
callers.consumption: n/a -- not part of the agent's decision path at all

web/counterfactual_analyzer.py:analyze_c.decision_effect: NO_CODE_REFERENCE from main.py's perspective -- this module is never imported by the agent
web/counterfactual_analyzer.py:analyze_c.notes: Included in this matrix for completeness (it was named in the roadmap's PR0-C candidate list) but EXCLUDED from shadow comparison: it does not evaluate a Snapshot, it post-hoc analyzes recorded disagreements between the agent's ranking and a human's choice across whole games.

included: _eval_search_state (requires one engine rollout per candidate per hidden-sample; explicitly single-sample unless run with multiple hidden states, in which case CRN caveats from PR0-B apply)
value_model.predict_action_value (cheap if model files are present, independent of use_value_model gate for shadow-only purposes)
excluded: evaluate_state (per-state, not per-candidate -- has no candidate ranking to compare; its dead-code status is already fully characterized by PR0-A.1)
web/counterfactual_analyzer.py (offline, cross-game, not a per-decision evaluator)
explicitly_not_implemented_by_PR0C: no change to any evaluator's formula
no change to any selected action in PRODUCTION or BENCHMARK mode
